content.title: Yankees blank Giants in blowout MLB Opening Day win: Score, highlights
content.text: SAN FRANCISCO — The 2026 Major League Baseball regular season began at Oracle Park on Wednesday night with the San Francisco Giants hosting the New York Yankees.It was all New York, all game.The Yankees notched a 7-0 victory against the Giants in front of a sellout crowd of 40,856 who gathered to the Bay Area for MLB Opening Day.AdvertisementIt was the first game for Giants new manager Tony Vitello, who was hired in October following seven seasons as coach for the Tennessee Volunteers.The Yankees really took off in the second inning, connecting on five hits for five runs. Giancarlo Stanton went 2-for-4 with an RBI, Austin Wells was 2-for-3, and Ryan McMahon provided two RBIs in the game. Trent Grisham drove in two runs and Jose Caballero added an RBI.1 / 7Baseball returns as Yankees, Giants face off in start to MLB seasonA general view as a smoke flag fires during the national anthem before the game between the San Francisco Giants and the New York Yankees on Opening Day at Oracle Park on March 25, 2026 in San Francisco, Calif.2 / 7Baseball returns as Yankees, Giants face off in start to MLB seasonLogan Webb of the San Francisco Giants pitches against the New York Yankees during the first inning on Opening Day at Oracle Park on March 25, 2026 in San Francisco, Calif.7 / 7Baseball returns as Yankees, Giants face off in start to MLB seasonNetflix Broadcaster and NFL Quarterback Jameis Winston interviews Aaron Judge #99 of the New York Yankees before the game against the San Francisco Giants on Opening Day at Oracle Park on March 25, 2026 in San Francisco, Calif.The only Yankees player to not register a hit was reigning AL MVP Aaron Judge, who was struck out four times in the Opening Day game.It was a rough outing for Giants starting pitcher Logan Webb. Webb delivered 86 pitches, 58 for strikes, with seven strikeouts in over five innings. He allowed nine hits, seven runs, six earned runs, a walk and hit a batter.AdvertisementThis Opening Day marked the regular-season debut of MLB's new automated balls and strikes (ABS) system that allows players to challenge balls and strikes.Here's how the opener unfolded.8th innning: Giants 0, Yankees 7Yankees had zero hits in the eighth. Brubaker struck out McMahon, Wells flew out to center and Grisham was grounded out to second.It was a lot of the same for the Giants. They got an eighth inning hit from Arraez, which extended his consecutive hit streak to 16 games, the longest in MLB. Chapman was walked to first, but that was about it for San Francisco. Devers at bat following Chapman ended the inning with a flyout at center.Advertisement7th inning: Giants 0, Yankees 7JT Brubaker took the mound in the seventh inning. He struck out Stanton. Brubaker only allowed one hit, a Chisholm single. Cabarello was next grounded out, into a double play as Chisholm was out at second. Yankees' Jake Bird replaced Max Fried, who finished with four strikeouts and allowed just two hits in 6.1 innings pitched.6th inning: Giants 0, Yankees 7Giants faithful haven't had much to cheer for all game. The biggest highlight for San Francisco is that they have struck out reigning AL MVP Aaron Judge four times through the sixth inning.Webb got him three times in the previous but was shut down for the night after the fifth.Giants ace Logan Webb's night should be over after throwing 86 pitches over five innings, and down 7-0.Webb's line:5 innings9 hits7 runs6 earned runs1 walk7 strikeouts1 hit batter.86 pitches, 58 strikes.— Bob Nightengale (@BNightengale) March 26, 2026Keaton Winn took over at the top of the sixth and got himself a strikeout on Judge. That's one bragging right for San Francisco, other than they haven't had much to be gleeful about.Aaron Judge just struck out for the fourth time in four at-bats in six innings.He's only the third Yankee to strike out 4 times on opening day.And yet...Yankees 7, Giants 0.— Bob Nightengale (@BNightengale) March 26, 2026In the bottom of the sixth inning Chapman, Devers and Adames all lined out to go to the seventh.AdvertisementYankees' second baseman showed off his quick reflexes to get Chapman out. Chisholm caught a line drive that came right at him. He bobbled the initial catch with his glove before making the catch with his bare hand.5th inning: Giants 0, Yankees 7Cody Bellinger got the fifth inning warmed up with a single to right field. Rice followed with a single which would help to set up a RBI from Stanton. He took one to center which made way for Bellinger to go home. Chisholm grounded to first, but an error throw from Willy Adames and miscalculated grab by Schmitt allowed Rice to score.4th inning: Giants 0, Yankees 5History was made in the fourth inning. The first-ever ABS challenge was initiated by Yankees shortstop Jose Caballero. He lost. The umpire upheld the call. But it was short moment to behold, alas the ABS finally happened.Jose Caballero makes the first challenge in ABS history.And loses.— Bob Nightengale (@BNightengale) March 26, 2026Apparently, the live viewers tuning in on Netflix missed out on the debut ABS challenge replay as the broadcast was conducting an in-game interview with Giants new manager Tony Vitello.The Yankees didn't score any runs in the fourth, but also held San Francisco without any runs, despite Heliot Ramos hitting a single to right field. Schmitt hit a ground ball to center field, as Ramos was tagged out at second base.Advertisement3rd inning: Giants 0, Yankees 5San Francisco was able to the Yankees off the bat and back on defense rather swiftly in the third inning. Webb delivered a couple of strikeouts against Stanton and Ben Rice.Chisholm grounded out at first.Giants were still looking for something to get going offensively but they could not find a flow. Arraez was grounded out at first, Matt Chapman flied out and Devers was also grounded out as Yankees took over heading into the fourth inning.2nd inning: Giants 0, Yankees 5Yankees went on a flurry in the second inning which was kicked off by consecutive hits a the plate. Giancarlo Stanton knocked a single to right field. Chisholm was automatically walked after being hit with a pitch from Webb.AdvertisementWith Stanton and Chisholm on first and second, a double to left field from Jose Caballero opened things up for New York allowing Stanton to cross home plate for the first score of the 2026 MLB season.The series of hits continued for the Yankees. Ryan McMahon followed Caballero with a single to center, earning two RBIs as Caballero and Chisholm both ran in scores.Austin Wells kept the momentum going, attacking center field. He and McMahon were on base, as Grisham made his second plate appearance. He tripled this time around, bringing home Wells and McMahon. New York built a 5-0 lead on five hits.The Giants didn't register a single hit in the second inning. One runner made base, Casey Schmitt, after being hit with a pitch.Advertisement1st inning: Giants 0, Yankees 0The Giants opened the season with a couple of Logan Webb strikeouts, sending Trent Grisham and Aaron Judge back to the dugout. Giants were off the field and on to the bottom of the inning after getting Cody Bellinger out.Rafael Devers made contact and sent one over the head of second-baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. Grisham had to run it down but not before it could drop to the ground. Devers singled with one on base. Giants could not capitalize after Willy Adames was struck out and Jung Hoo Lee was grounded out.MLB season gets underwayBaseball is season is officially among us in this classic battle of east versus west between the Giants and Yankees. Both teams leaned into their city's history as the Giants brought trolleys, a historic means of transportation in San Francisco, on to the playing field as they introduced their starters.Yankees lineup was introduced running out of their dugout between taxi cabs with a "NY" logo near the rear while "Lean Back" by Fat Joe played on the ballpark's speakers. Giants opened the game with Logan Webb versus Trent Grisham at bat.AdvertisementWebb opened the 2026 season with a strikeout.Where to watch Giants vs YankeesTime: 8:05 p.m. ETLocation: Oracle Park, San Francisco1 / 30See the top 30 highest paid players in MLB baseball(Salaries in present-day value calculated by MLB Labor Relations Department, impacted by deferrals and signing bonuses)1.
